Assignments

Six assignments · 7% each

Each assignment has a checkpoint (20%) and a final submission (80%). Open one for its scope; the handout has starter code, tests, and submission instructions.

Capstone · 13% · in pairs

One question, two experiments.

Pick a data-systems or training-systems question, keep the data and model fixed, change one thing, and explain what you measure. A well-supported negative result earns full credit.

    Grading and policies

    Six assignments
    42%

    15%
    Final (cumulative)
    15%
    Capstone
    13%
    Five labs
    10%
    Weekly concept checks
    5%

    Exams test reasoning; practice exams are provided and you may bring one page of notes. Concept checks allow unlimited attempts and are graded for completion.

    Assignment grading

    Checkpoint 20%, final submission 80%. The final is assessed on correctness (about 50%), performance (about 20%), and analysis (about 30%). Performance credit requires correct code. After D3 and T3, you complete a ten-minute individual code walkthrough with staff.

    Late work and outages

    Five slip days per semester, at most two per submission, none on the capstone. Reference outputs are released 48 hours after each deadline, and no submissions are accepted after that. A cluster outage near a deadline moves the deadline.

    Collaboration and AI tools

    Discuss ideas freely; write your own code and analysis. Do not share or view others’ code, except with your capstone partner on the capstone. AI tools may explain concepts, read documentation, and help debug, but may not write the parts each handout assigns to you. Cite AI use, including prompts.

    Help and accommodations

    If you fall behind, start the next stage from a reference output. Recitation and office hours cover tools and concepts; a TA will contact you if you miss a checkpoint. For accommodations, register with the Disability Resource Center and talk with an instructor early. The Rice Honor Code applies. Test at small scale and release cluster resources when finished.

    Getting ready

    Who the course is for

    Juniors with a math and ML background who are curious about systems. GPU programming, frameworks, and cluster tools are taught from the ground up.

    Prerequisites (proposed): COMP 345 and linear algebra (CMOR 302, CMOR 303, MATH 221, MATH 354, or MATH 355), plus Python at the level of COMP 182. The current catalog lists COMP 215, 222, and 345.

    Before Jan 11

    A four-hour head start: refresh Python, NumPy, the terminal, and git, and review tensor shapes, the chain rule, and gradient-based optimization.

    • Complete the ungraded primer
    • Take the math and ML self-check
    • Activate your cluster account

    Materials and account instructions are on Canvas.
